mentl/1a7fc89:
Nine hand-closed comment families were one law fought site by site.
The inversion replaces them: attach_comment_weave runs once after
parse_program, resolving every comment run by span against the node
weave — trailing runs to the widest node starting on their line,
leading runs to the widest node at the minimal start past the run,
span ties to the latest mint (which retires the desugar transfer),
and a blank-separated earlier block inherits the next run's target.
One scan of the span index serves every run.

Emission went uniform at render_tokens_for: every node's attached
prose prefixes its own tokens, the per-construct emission calls
delete (rows keep theirs — op and variant carrier nodes never flow
through the entry), and prose-forced breaks cascade from fits_inline
seeing the emitted newline. The verb writes its own fixpoint — fmt
renders, re-parses, re-renders, and writes the second render — so
one invocation is idempotent by construction.

Roughly fifty parse and render sites delete whole, including the
probe-law contortions and the attach/collect helper family; the
parser's skips are comment-transparent again. The run record is
nominal (CwRun) because the generic bsearch walkers compile once and
an open element floored their field reads; the brand plus param
intent boundaries prove the offsets.

Conservation measured 1,969 to 741 to 106 lost lines across the
wheel, idempotent-all-50, whole board green. The working discipline
is reified in CLAUDE.md: Edit-tool-only source writes, the medium's
projections before shell reads, verbs carry their own fixpoints, the
uniform pass beats the per-site family.

mentl/1aeed27:
m3 assembly, past face 17, refused $__fanout_input_19472 at diverge_0:
the <| divergent-fanout thunk synthesis captured its shared input
wrong AND missed the branch's own free vars — two bugs, both from
hand-rolling a closure instead of using the >< path's machinery.

synthesize_diverge_thunks (<|) and synthesize_branch_thunk (><) were
two closure-synthesis disciplines for one thing; the seam was the bug.
The diverge thunk referenced the shared input as a bare LLocal (the
parent's let-local, undefined in the separate thunk fn) and captured
NONE of the branch's frees (a lambda branch's k, undefined too). Both
invisible because every fanout micro used >< — the <| path had ZERO
coverage.

Now one discipline: the diverge thunk captures via the same
collect_free_vars + resolve_captures_outer + frame that branch thunks
use, with the shared input as a synthetic slot-0 capture read as an
upval, and the branch lowered UNDER the frame so its own frees resolve
to upvals transitively. The seed's hand-WAT diverge was already
correct — this brings the wheel's lower up to it.

Two ratchets close the coverage gap: mn-diverge-share=105 (named-fn
branches), mn-diverge-lambda=125 (lambda branches capturing a free
var), both green both tiers.
